newsitem.title: UK: Coventry building society raises mortgage rates.
newsitem.headline: Coventry building society raises mortgage rates.

text.p: The Coventry, Britain's 12th largest building society, said on Monday it would raise its mortgage rates on January 1 1997 following the 1/4 point rise in UK base rate on October 30.
The Coventry's standard variable rate will rise to 7.25 percent from 6.99 percent.
The rise follows a move at the weekend by Abbey National Plc, which said it was raising its mortgage rates by 1/4 point.
Mortagage lenders had initially held their rates unchanged despite the October rise in bank base lending.

Britain's biggest mortgage lender, the Halifax Building Society, said on Monday it had no present plans to follow the Abbey move but was continuing to review rates. Last week, the Halifax said it would await developments at the next monetary meeting between Chancellor Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George, on December 11.

"The move in mortgage rates is necessary for the Coventry because we are determined to maintain our competitive rates of interest to savers," Coventry Chief Executive Martin Richley said in a statement.
